levels.low: No URL validation. The server fetches any URL submitted by the user, resolving it against an in-process registry of fake internal services.
levels.medium: Blocklist of exact IP/hostname strings (127.0.0.1, localhost, 169.254.169.254). Flaw: internal service hostnames and alternate IP encodings are not in the blocklist.
levels.high: Hostname allowlist enforced. Flaw: HTTP redirects are followed without re-validating the redirect target against the allowlist — SSRF via open redirect.
levels.impossible: Allowlist enforced; scheme must be https; redirects are never followed. Not exploitable.

hints.low: The server will fetch any URL you give it. What internal services might be reachable that are not meant to be public?
hints.medium: Some hostnames are blocked by name. Can you reach an internal service using its hostname directly instead of an IP address?
hints.high: The allowlist looks solid. But what happens after the allowed server responds? Does the client follow the server's redirect without checking where it leads?
hints.impossible: Nothing to bypass here. Compare what the impossible level does differently with redirects and URL validation.

low.note: POST url=http://internal-metadata/latest/meta-data/ to reach the fake metadata service.

medium.note: The hostname blocklist does not cover all internal service names. Try service hostnames directly.

high.note: Find an allowed host that issues a redirect to an internal service, then submit that host's URL.

impossible.note: No bypass available at impossible level.
